subject: Polity
description: Vidhan Sabha, Vidhan Parishad, CM, SC/HC interface

questions.stem: How many Indian states currently have a bicameral legislature (Vidhan Sabha + Vidhan Parishad)?
questions.explanation: Six bicameral states (as of 2025): Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh. All others are unicameral. Creating or abolishing a Vidhan Parishad requires a state-legislature resolution followed by a Parliament Act (Art 169). J&K had a Council until 2019 reorganisation.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The normal term of a Vidhan Sabha (State Legislative Assembly) is:
questions.explanation: Art 172 — Vidhan Sabha has a 5-year term unless dissolved earlier by the Governor on the CM's advice, or during President's Rule. Strength: 60 to 500 members (Art 170). Smaller states have fewer: Sikkim 32, Goa 40, Mizoram 40. Rajya Sabha / Vidhan Parishad are permanent bodies with 6-year member terms.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of the Vidhan Parishad (State Legislative Council)?

options.option_text: It is dissolved with the Vidhan Sabha
One-third of its members retire every two years
One-half of its members retire every three years
All members are directly elected by the people

questions.explanation: Like Rajya Sabha, the Vidhan Parishad is a permanent body — 1/3 retire every 2 years, each member serves 6 years. Max strength = 1/3 of the Vidhan Sabha. Composition: 1/3 by MLAs, 1/3 by local bodies, 1/12 by teachers, 1/12 by registered graduates, the rest nominated by the Governor (literature, science, art, social service).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The minimum age to be elected as an MLA (Vidhan Sabha member) is:
questions.explanation: Art 173 — MLA minimum age is 25, same as Lok Sabha MP. MLC / Rajya Sabha MP — 30. President, Vice-President, Governor — 35. Voting age — 18 (reduced from 21 by the 61st Amendment, 1988).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Governor of a state is appointed by the:
questions.explanation: Art 155 — Governors are appointed by the President. Art 156 — holds office during the pleasure of the President (no formal removal procedure; 5-year term by convention). Must be a citizen of India aged 35+. Oath of office administered by the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court (Art 159).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The retirement age of a High Court judge is:
questions.explanation: HC judges retire at 62 (raised from the original 60 by the 15th Amendment, 1963). SC judges retire at 65. HC judges are appointed by the President after consultation with the CJI, the HC Chief Justice, and the Governor of the state (Art 217).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States (Art 246) is laid down in which Schedule of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Seventh Schedule contains three lists — Union List (~100 subjects: defence, foreign affairs, atomic energy), State List (~61: police, land, public health), Concurrent List (~52: both may legislate, Union prevails on conflict). Fourth = Rajya Sabha seat allocation; Eighth = scheduled languages (22); Eleventh = panchayat subjects (29, via 73rd Amendment).
